t: The Maratha Empire grew from Shivaji's hill forts in the Western Ghats into a confederacy that dominated 18th-century India.
It broke Mughal supremacy, reaching Attock on the Indus in 1758 and later controlling Delhi and the Mughal emperor.
Defeat at Panipat in 1761, rivalry among its chiefs and three wars with the East India Company ended its independence in 1818.
dyk: The Marathas built a capable navy with sea forts such as Sindhudurg; under Kanhoji Angre in the early 18th century it challenged even the English and Dutch.
ev: Shivaji captures the fort of Torna, beginning his rise
Shivaji kills the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad
Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad, formally asserting sovereignty
Shivaji's son Sambhaji is executed during the long war with Aurangzeb
Peshwa Baji Rao I defeats the Nizam at Palkhed
Maratha armies reach Attock on the Indus
The Durrani army of Ahmad Shah Abdali crushes the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat
Peshwa Baji Rao II surrenders to the British and the Peshwa's office is abolished
